solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Latin tutor's admission of responsibility?

parts.note: a teacher of the classical tongue owning up would naturally use that language's own phrase for 'my fault'

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster owns up to some blunder in class.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is a playful description: a Latin teacher confessing would say it in Latin, with the familiar two-word phrase meaning 'through my fault'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase, literally 'my fault', is used in English as an open confession of blame.

clue.text: Same kit reused? That's an oversight

indicators.note: putting the letters to fresh use in a new order signals rearranging them

explanation.surface: Someone wore the same kit twice, a blunder in a sports team's wardrobe.
explanation.definitionFit: An oversight is an error made through inattention, the same as a slip or blunder.

clue.text: Strength of a Hardy heroine from the south

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading up from the bottom means the name is turned backwards

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Thomas Hardy's best-known heroine

explanation.surface: Praising the resilience of a character from Thomas Hardy's novels, a woman from the south of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A strength in the sense of a useful quality or advantage is a valuable resource.

clue.text: No big deal, as Norman put it after mix-up

indicators.note: the words are presented as what results once they are jumbled, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a muddle, quoting a man named Norman.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is no big deal is trivial, of little consequence.

clue.text: Took a quick look, annoyed you might say

indicators.note: points to how a word is spoken rather than written

parts.note: piqued means irritated or resentful

explanation.surface: Someone glanced briefly, irritated at what they saw.
explanation.definitionFit: To peek is to glance furtively or briefly at something.

clue.text: Hear, moving right to front, a flightless bird

indicators.note: says one letter of the given word is shifted to another place
names where that letter goes: to the start of the word

explanation.surface: An instruction to listen, then something about a flightless bird on the move.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large South American ratite, related to the ostrich and unable to fly.

clue.text: Dishy school principal, an impetuous person

parts.note: dishy is informal for attractive, as is hot
the head teacher of a school

explanation.surface: An attractive headmaster who acts rashly.
explanation.definitionFit: A hothead is someone rash, quick-tempered and acting without thought.

clue.text: Check car will be on time

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting on top of another places it first

parts.note: Audi is a German car make

explanation.surface: Reassurance that a car will arrive punctually.
explanation.definitionFit: An audit is an official inspection or examination, especially of accounts.

clue.text: Omnivorous US hillbillies eating this?

indicators.note: the words take the answer inside them, as if it were their food

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the whole second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Mountain folk who will eat anything might even try raw-fish dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish, the sort of food even unfussy eaters might balk at.

clue.text: Delighted Conservative, left outside

indicators.note: the word for left sits around the abbreviation

parts.note: exited means went out, departed

explanation.surface: A Tory delighted after leaving the party.
explanation.definitionFit: Excited and delighted both describe a state of thrilled, happy anticipation.

clue.text: Strange career he led, this enthusiastic supporter

indicators.note: an odd arrangement of the letters signals rearranging them

explanation.surface: Commenting on the odd career someone led as a keen supporter.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheerleader leads the crowd's cheering, and figuratively is anyone who champions a cause.

clue.text: Fancy leaving wife for social worker?

indicators.note: the abbreviation for wife departs from the word

parts.note: to fancy something is to want it

explanation.surface: Someone wanting to leave a wife for a member of the caring professions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' looks like a job title, but the definition plays on ants as social insects that work in colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: Ants are social insects, and worker ants are the colony's labourers.

clue.text: Repented raving about Charlie in previous case

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the letter for Charlie
wild, delirious behaviour signals the letters of the next word being jumbled

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone repented, raving about a man called Charlie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raving' turns REPENTED into PREEDENT, and 'about' places that around C.
explanation.definitionFit: A precedent is an earlier decided case taken as a guide for later ones, especially in law.

clue.text: Accept some stolen Dürers

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A demand to accept the theft of some paintings by the German artist Dürer.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure something is to tolerate or put up with it.

clue.text: Corrupt deputy, half gone at party

indicators.note: with half of it gone, only the first three of the word's six letters are kept

parts.note: a rave is a large party with dance music

explanation.surface: A dishonest deputy, half-cut at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To deprave is to corrupt someone morally.

clue.text: Bachelor, a learner, keeping clear of wedding?

indicators.note: the outer letters hold the word for clear within them

parts.note: L is for learner, as on a British learner driver's L-plate
rid as in 'get rid of' means clear

explanation.surface: A single man learning to steer clear of marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridal means relating to a bride or a wedding, as in a bridal party.

clue.text: Boat that's not so heavy

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a flat-bottomed barge used to unload ships
second meaning: comparative of light, weighing less

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are unrelated words spelt the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighter is a barge that ferries cargo, and the comparative of light describes less weight.

clue.text: One recording beer drinkers downing last of ale

indicators.note: the drinkers swallow the letter, so it goes inside them

parts.note: CAMRA is the Campaign for Real Ale, a British organisation of beer enthusiasts

indicators.note: takes only the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A device capturing beer drinkers knocking back the dregs of their ale.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera is an apparatus that records images on film or digitally.

clue.text: "A Greek", this leading chap?

parts.note: alpha is the Greek letter corresponding to A
a chap is a man, a male

explanation.surface: Pointing out a Greek man who leads the pack.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, the clue also describes the answer: alpha, the first Greek letter, stands for being first, so this chap leads.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpha male is the dominant man in a group, the one who leads the others.

clue.text: Confused, as Columbus often was?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: bewildered, not knowing what to do
second meaning: literally on the ocean, as the explorer was on his voyages

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal reading: Columbus spent long voyages on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for bewildered literally means out on the ocean, where a navigator like Columbus spent months.

clue.text: Go back with husband, a greedy fellow

indicators.note: here 'with' joins the abbreviation for husband to the reversed word, the abbreviation going first
the word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wife telling a selfish man to return home with her spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Hog is slang for a greedy person who takes more than a fair share.

clue.text: Caught a lot of cattle, they say

indicators.note: points to how a word is spoken rather than written

parts.note: a herd is a group of cattle

explanation.surface: Rustlers caught with a large number of cattle, according to rumour.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch what someone said is to hear it.

clue.text: Surprise the French after kick-off

indicators.note: the French word follows the word for kick-off

parts.note: the kick-off is the start of a football match
le is French for the

explanation.surface: French opponents caught out right after a match begins.
explanation.definitionFit: To startle is to give someone a sudden shock or fright.

clue.text: Republican in silly plan

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes inside the word for silly

parts.note: daft is British informal for silly

explanation.surface: A Republican caught up in a foolish scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a preliminary version or outline of a plan or document.

clue.text: A risky venture? Help!

parts.note: a bet is a gamble, a risky undertaking

explanation.surface: A cry for assistance after a gamble goes wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to assist or encourage, usually in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Brad in LA, or somewhere in Canada?

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a man named Brad is in Los Angeles or in Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue words simply run together in order: LA, then BRAD, then OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Labrador is the mainland region of the Canadian province of Newfoundland and Labrador.
